sentences.text: THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE N.V.SHRAVAN KUMAR  WRIT PETITION No.15141 of 2025 ORDER:

This writ petition is filed seeking following prayer:-
"to declare the action of the 5th Respondent in not allowing the petitioner to serve flavored herbal hookah to the customers and also obstructing the business activities of the cafe and acting further in contravention of the principles of natural justice as illegal, arbitrary, and it is further prayed that this Honourable Court pending disposal of the writ petition may be pleased to direct the respondents not to obstruct the business activities of the petitioner and allow them to serve flavored herbal Hookah to the customers of his cafe."
2. Brief facts stated in this writ petition are that petitioner is a coffee shop running under the name and style of M/s.Sky Line, situated at Gundlapochampally, Kandlakoi Village, Medchal Malkajgiri District.

It is stated that the petitioner, having acquired the statutory licenses from the competent authorities which includes registration of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Municipal Trade License, Labour License, is running the said business.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further stated that the said shop is also serving hooka to the customers.

The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No.5 under Section 7(5) and 21(1) of COTPA Act 2003, registered FIR No.672 of 2025 dated 16.04.2025 against the petitioner and during the investigation visited the subject premises and seized the hookah pots.
Thereafter, notice under Section 35(3)of BNSS was issued to the petitioner.
It is further stated that petitioner has not violated any of the provisions of COTPA Act 2003.
Further case of the petitioner is that the respondent authorities are entering the petitioner's subject premises and are threatening to seal the same.
Aggrieved by the same, this writ petition is filed.

3. Today when the matter has been taken up for hearing, learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court to the order dated 08.12.2022 passed in W.P.No.15944 of 2022,
relevant portion is extracted hereunder:-
"6.

Though the Act does not contemplate any licence to be taken, in the larger interest of the youngsters, who are visiting the hookah centres, the restaurant owners shall have a definite place for hookah / smoking.

The restaurant owners, who are having a separate place for smoking and for hookah consumption, shall inform the same to the Station House Officer, so that they can have surveillance on the activities that are taking place in the said place and whether the business is carried out as per the norms and the procedure laid down under the Act.

Police under the guise of this,
shall not harass the persons running these centers without following the procedure.
The officers, who are competent alone can enter the premises.

If there is any high-handed action on the part of the police, the same shall be brought to the notice M/S Sky Line vs The State Of Telangana on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139296528/
1 of the higher authorities and they shall cause enquiry into the same and take appropriate action.

sentences.text: 7 . The Writ Petition is accordingly, disposed of.

No order as to costs."
4.

Relying on the above, learned counsel for the petitioner pray this Court to grant liberty to petitioner to make representation before the respondent Police and seek permission to serve hookah at his cafe.
5. Sri.
M.Srinivas
, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 5 pray this Court to pass appropriate order.
6. Heard and perused the material available on record.

On perusal of the Registration Certificate issued under FSS Act, 2006, by the Government of Telangana, it is noticed that the kind of petitioner's business is classified as petty retailer of snacks/tea shops and the food category to be served at the petitioner's premises is mentioned as prepared foods and dairy products.
It is further noticed that in the Certificate of Registration, issued by the Government of Telangana, the nature of business is mentioned as coffee shop.

7. At this stage, it is relevant to refer to the paragraph No.5 of the order dated 08.12.2022 passed in W.P.No.15944 of 2022 and the same is extracted hereunder:-
"5.
There cannot be any dispute with regard to the fact that police have the power to regulate smoking in a public place in the manner specified as provided under Sections 4 & 12 of the Act.
In some cases, the owners of the restaurants contend that they have licence from GHMC.

Though they have a trade licence from GHMC,
ultimately, as per the power conferred under the Act, it is the respective police who have the authority to regulate and monitor.

Further, the object of the Act is to prohibit consumption of cigarette and other tobacco products which are injurious to health and in the larger interest of improving the public health, as per Article 47 of the Constitution of India which deals with the duty of the State to protect the public health.

It is also observed that most of the restaurants which obtained trade licence for the purpose of running a restaurant or cafeteria are converting the same into hookah parlours for running hookah centres.

As per Section 4 of the Act, a separate place is required to be maintained for restaurants which have the capacity of 30 seats,
that ipso facto will not give any right to the restaurant owners to run the hookah parlours.

At the place of smoking, except smoking, no other service shall be allowed and if basing on the permission granted for a restaurant, they are only running hookah centres, the authorities have a right to cancel the licence.

Invariably, the police have to have constant check and control whether the concerned are following the provisions of the Act and the Rules and whether they are displaying statutory and pictorial warning notices.

As per Section 12 of the COTP Act, the police not below the rank of Sub-Inspector or any officer of State Food or Drug Administration or any other officer, holding the equivalent rank being not below the rank of Sub-Inspector M/S Sky Line vs The State Of Telangana on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139296528/
2
of Police, authorised by the Central Government or by the State Government can inspect any building.
In view of the same, there cannot be any direction from this Court to the respondents not to visit hookah centres of the petitioner.
It has come to light that under the guise of hookah parlour, in some cases, they are getting the customers used to the other narcotic drugs.
Even on that ground also, there should be constant surveillance and check by the police.

There should be a fine balance from the respondent police where they can only interfere in the business when there is a statutory violation or any incidents that are contrary to law are taking place in the said premises, but under the guise of it, the police just like that cannot harass the persons who are running the hookah centres.
If there is any high-handed action on the part of the officer, the same can be brought to the notice of the higher authorities and the higher authorities shall take appropriate action.

The petitioner shall earmark exclusively a separate area with appropriate enclosure in the hotel premises and no other area or portion of the premises shall be used by the customers of the petitioner for smoking hookah."

8. It is also relevant to refer to the common order dated 15.11.2023 passed in W.P.Nos.8223 of 2013 and batch, relevant portion is extracted hereunder:-
"ii) Since the Hyderabad City Police Act, 1348 Fasli confers power over the amusement Centres/restaurants which are defined as "public place"
under the COTP Act and as per Rule 4 of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008 permission is required specifying smoking area.

entities.text: Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, to establish hookah centres, the petitioners shall obtain necessary permission from the concerned authority under the provisions of the City Police Act."

9. Having considered the above facts and circumstances and recording the submissions made by the learned counsel on either side, this writ petition is disposed of granting liberty to petitioner to make representation before the respondent Police, seeking permission to serve hookah at his cafe and in the light of order dated 08.12.2022 passed in W.P.No.15944 of 2022 and common order dated 15.11.2023 passed in W.P.Nos.8223 of 2013, respondent authorities are directed to pass appropriate orders strictly in accordance with law and communicate the same to the petitioner.

It is made clear that this Court had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case, it is for the respondent authorities to pass appropriate orders for permission strictly in accordance with law.
Needless to say that the respondent authorities shall follow due procedure as contemplated under law before initiating any action against the petitioner.
10. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

JUSTICE N.V.SHRAVAN KUMAR Date:
